newsitem.title: HUNGARY: EBRD MAY RAISE HUNGARY K&H BANK CAPITAL BY $30 MLN.
newsitem.headline: EBRD MAY RAISE HUNGARY K&H BANK CAPITAL BY $30 MLN.

text.p: The European Bank of Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) will raise the capital of Hungary's Kereskedelmi Bank (K&H) by $30 million if a future strategic investor in Kereskedelmi agrees, K&H said on Friday.

"We managed to conclude a preliminary contract with the EBRD whereby the EBRD will raise K&H's capital in the form of a $30 million subordinated loan, if their board of directors and our shareholders' meeting approves," Eros said.
The state plans to sell an at least 25 percent plus one vote stake in K&H, which has an 11 percent share of the Hungarian banking market, to a strategic investor this year.
The EBRD's capital increase is subject to the agreement of the new strategic investor, Eros said.
"(The capital increase) depends on whether the strategic investor wants EBRD to be part of the bank," he said.
So far 10 investors have bought the tender prostectus for K&H's privatisation, while others are likely to purchase it later, Eros said.
"There is very serious interest in the bank," he said.

The pre-qualification period of the tender will be closed on April 11 and the state privatisation agency APV will decide in two weeks which three to six investors will go forward to the second round, he added.
Eros said the investors expressed special interest in the bank's retail business branch.

Analysts see competition for retail banking customers sharpening in Hungary as foreign investors which bought domestic banks recently, including Dutch ABN-Amro and ING and Germany's DG Bank all plan to carve substantial market share.

Bank officials could not immediately disclose market share statistics, but said that K&H was one of the largest retail banks in Hungary, with the deposits of individuals totalling some 150 billion forints.
The bank increased its balance sheet total to 360 billion forints in 1996 from 326.8 billion in 1995, while average inflation was 23.6 percent last year, the bank said in a statement.
After-tax profits grew to 2.7 billion forints last year from 1.9 billion forints in 1995, it said.
The figures are audited and were calculated according to Hungarian accounting standards.
